title: Persistent Memory Skills
description: How to use Gotcha persistent memory under Gotcha/memory.
instructions:
Gotcha persistent memory lives under Gotcha/memory next to chats. SOUL.md is identity and behavior. MEMORY.md is the master map with navigational addresses, never facts. user.md is synced from Settings Personal Info. Detail lives in people/, areas/, notes/. Raw drops (uploads, audio, images, documents in any format) live in raw/.

Session start: SOUL.md and MEMORY.md are already injected as [memory_startup] with absolute paths. Follow them for the whole chat. Load detail files only when the task needs them, with read_file or grep using ABSOLUTE paths. Never resolve memory paths relative to the chat working directory, which is a different folder. Never bulk read the folder.

Record schema: every file you create in people/, areas/ or notes/ MUST start with YAML frontmatter between --- lines: required title, area, type (person, note, meeting, decision, reference, area, contact-card), updated (ISO yyyy-MM-dd). Optional tags (slug list like [k99, cerebral-palsy]), source, source_file, stage, project, summary, next_action (the one concrete follow-up), task_ref (a scheduled task id). area uses the MEMORY.md vocabulary (starts as People, Work, Personal, Health). Types belong to directories: areas/ holds type area hubs, people/ holds type person cards, notes/ holds note, meeting, decision or reference. tags are lowercase slugs: letters, digits and single hyphens only, never spaces, capitals or underscores. Writes with bad frontmatter are rejected by the tool with the reasons: fix them and retry. Facts live in the body with [[links]], never in the map.

Digest workflow: when the user shares or uploads a file worth keeping, classify it. A durable insight becomes a note with frontmatter (source_file naming the raw file plus a [[raw/...]] link in a Sources section). Copy small or at-risk files into raw/ with write_file. Files over ~10 MB already on durable disk are linked in place: record the absolute path, never duplicate them. Never link temp, cache or staging paths: even huge files there must be copied into raw/ when the user asks to keep them. Always ask whether to keep the raw copy: yes means file it with a one-line description recorded in the owning note and MEMORY.md, no means digest from the given path without copying. Raw files are immutable: never edit, only delete once digested AND linked. Propose cleanup of raw files older than 30 days instead of letting them pile up. Trivial drops are deleted, never filed.

Task links: when a note commits to dated work, create the scheduled task with schedule_agent_task passing memory_note (the note's absolute path), and write the approved task id back into the note's task_ref frontmatter plus the concrete follow-up into next_action. Link both ways or not at all: a task whose note is deleted gets its link cleared with edit_scheduled_task, and a note whose task is deleted loses its task_ref. The viewer flags notes pointing at unknown task ids. A ready-made Morning briefing preset (MONITOR, daily, read-only, writes the structured day plan as its chat response) ships paused in Settings / Scheduled tasks: the user enables it.

Duplicate guard: before creating a person, area or note, grep memory for the name and compare slugs ("Asha Sharma" is asha-sharma). If a card or note already covers it, update that file instead of creating a second one. One fact in one place.

History rule: dated notes (names starting yyyy-MM-dd) describe what was true THEN. Never rewrite their bodies when decisions change. New decisions go in new notes with a Superseded by [[path]] line at the top, linked both ways.

Timezone: the device timezone is truth. Resolve every user-facing date and time in it with zone-aware conversion (never a hardcoded offset: it breaks at each DST changeover). Write absolute dates (2026-10-29) in notes, never relative ones.

Link nodes whenever possible: every note, person, area and raw file you create or update must link to the related nodes with Obsidian-style [[links]] (for example [[people/asha-sharma.md]] or [[notes/trip-plan.md]]), and update MEMORY.md so the graph stays connected. One fact in one place: link, never copy-paste content. The viewer draws these links as a node graph, so an unlinked file is an invisible island. The viewer shows a health row (unlinked files, dangling links, records failing the schema, notes pointing at deleted tasks): work through it when the user asks for a cleanup.

Writes: OPERATOR only with write_file or edit using absolute paths. In MONITOR, read only, never write. Operator memory writes happen silently without a separate approval step: say briefly what was remembered so the user can correct it. Destructive actions (delete, or rewriting a dated note) still need explicit confirmation first. Never store passwords, OTPs, API tokens, or private keys anywhere in memory. Keep SOUL.md under 1500 chars and MEMORY.md under 1500 chars so session start stays cheap.

Areas start as People, Work, Personal, Health. You may rename, add, or archive an area by editing MEMORY.md plus its hub file in areas/. To create a new area, write areas/<name>.md first with area: <Name>, then file notes under it. Update MEMORY.md counts and links when you add a note that starts or advances a thread.
